---
title: "Disclosure determined by tier sizes"
subtitle: "3.2 · after the postrank theory book, ch. 9, 16 and 17"
description: "Combinatorial disclosure counts and their distribution over ordered positive size vectors."
---

The sizes of the tiers determine the number of stated pairs. All pairs between different tiers are stated, while
all within-tier pairs are withheld. The resulting disclosure count depends on the size vector but not on the
identities or posterior distributions of the units. The examples compare balanced and unbalanced vectors at fixed
unit and tier counts. The distribution enumerates ordered positive size patterns, rather than assignments of labelled
units to grades. It therefore describes a combinatorial property of reporting, independently of the accuracy of the
directions a particular assignment would state.

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Balanced thirty.** Sizes 10, 10, 10 state 300 of 435 pairs, a share of .690. Each withheld triangle contributes
  its within-tier count to the grouped formula. Balanced sizes reach the maximum for this number of tiers.
- **Two tiny tiers.** Sizes 1, 1, 28 state only 57 pairs, although they use the same number of tiers. The balanced
  reference still states 300. Moving the smallest tiers to another position gives the same disclosure but another
  ordered size pattern.
- **Four tiers.** Sizes 8, 7, 8, 7 state 337 pairs (.775). Equal sizes are impossible here. The balanced maximum
  still exists, while the closed form for equal-sized tiers is hidden.
- **Balanced twelve.** Three groups of four state 48 of 66 pairs. Valid size changes preserve the total unit count; the vector and individual controls specify the same setting.
- **Unbalanced twelve.** Sizes 5, 4, 3 state 47 pairs, below the balanced maximum of 48. A zero size or incorrect total is invalid; the result remains unavailable until the vector is feasible.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
The distribution gives equal weight to every ordered positive size vector for the declared unit and tier counts.
Its frequencies count size patterns rather than labelled grade reports. All feasible patterns are included; unit assignments are not enumerated. Quantile positions produce nearly balanced sizes when estimates have no
ties. The package keeps equal scores together, which can merge tiers and change the realised sizes. The formula's
count of disclosed pairs is exact for any valid sizes, with no posterior or accuracy guarantee.
:::
